# cockroach_sql_role (Resource)

CockroachDB SQL role.

A role groups privileges. Set `login` to also make it a principal that can authenticate, which is how a service account is provisioned without granting `admin`. Unlike `cockroach_sql_user`, a role starts with no privileges at all.

Every operation opens a SQL connection to the cluster, so `terraform apply` fails while the cluster is paused.

## Example Usage

```terraform
variable "cluster_id" {
  type = string
}

# A grouping role. It holds no privileges of its own and cannot log in;
# it exists so that privileges can be granted once and shared.
resource "cockroach_sql_role" "app_writer" {
  name       = "app_writer"
  cluster_id = var.cluster_id
}

# A principal that can log in. Unlike cockroach_sql_user, this credential
# starts with no privileges at all, which is what makes it usable for a
# service account scoped to a single application.
#
# password_wo is a write-only attribute (Terraform CLI 1.11+): its value is
# sent on create and on every rotation but is never stored in Terraform
# state. Sourcing it from an ephemeral input (for example, an ephemeral
# resource or a sensitive variable) keeps it out of state entirely.
#
# password_wo_version is the rotation trigger. Because the write-only value
# is not in state, Terraform cannot see a change to password_wo on its own;
# bump password_wo_version to signal that the new password should be
# applied. Pair every change to password_wo with a bump of this integer.
variable "ory_password" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
}

resource "cockroach_sql_role" "ory" {
  name                = "ory_service"
  login               = true
  password_wo         = var.ory_password
  password_wo_version = 1
  cluster_id          = var.cluster_id
}

# login can be toggled in place: flipping it to false revokes the ability to
# authenticate without destroying the role or the privileges granted to it.
# A password on a role with login = false is accepted and simply has no
# effect until login is granted again.
#
# A role with login = true and no password can still authenticate with a
# client certificate.
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `cluster_id` (String) The ID of the cluster the role belongs to.
- `name` (String) SQL role name. CockroachDB folds unquoted identifiers, so the name is lowercased before use. Reserved principals such as `admin`, `root` and `public` are rejected.

### Optional

- `login` (Boolean) Whether the role can authenticate. Defaults to `false`, which creates a role that groups privileges and cannot connect. This can be toggled in place; it never forces a replacement.
- `password_wo` (String, Sensitive) Write-only password for the role (Terraform CLI 1.11+ required). The value is sent on create and on rotation but is never stored in Terraform state. To rotate, change the value and bump `password_wo_version`; without a version bump, Terraform cannot detect changes to a write-only attribute. A password on a role with `login = false` is accepted and has no effect until login is granted.
- `password_wo_version` (Number) Trigger attribute for rotating `password_wo`. Increment this integer to force Terraform to re-apply the current `password_wo` value. Required when `password_wo` is set.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) A unique identifier with format `<cluster ID>:<SQL role name>`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

```shell
# format: <cluster id>:<sql role name>
terraform import cockroach_sql_role.app_writer 1f69fdd2-600a-4cfc-a9ba-16995df0d77d:app_writer
```
